blocks.text: **The problem.** Given a string `s`, sort its characters in **decreasing order of frequency** — the characters that appear most come first, with all copies of a character together. Characters with the same frequency can come in any order. Uppercase and lowercase are different characters.

blocks.alt: tree has counts e 2, t 1, r 1. Sorted by count, e comes first, then t and r in either order, giving eetr or eert.

elements.text: sort the characters by count, biggest first, then write each count times

blocks.text: The idea: count, then order the counts

Count every character with a hash map. Now the question is just about ordering the **distinct characters** by count — a custom comparator (biggest count first) does it in O(k log k) for k distinct characters. Then write each character out as many times as it appears.

Counts are whole numbers from 1 to n, so a **bucket sort** can replace the comparison sort: bucket `f` holds the characters that appear exactly `f` times, and reading the buckets from n down to 1 gives the right order in O(n).
1. Count, then sort the characters by count

blocks.caption: Count each character, sort the distinct characters by count, then expand them.

blocks.text: **Time O(n + k log k), space O(n)**, where k is the number of distinct characters — at most 62 letters and digits, so effectively O(n).
**Time O(n), space O(n).** No comparisons at all — the counts themselves are the positions.

blocks.alt: Sort by count: O(n + k log k) time, O(n) space. Buckets by count: O(n) time, O(n) space.

blocks.text: For letters only, k is tiny and both are linear in practice; the bucket version is the one to mention when k could be large.

items: **Ties** — `"cccaaa"`: either order is accepted, but each character's copies must stay together.
**Upper and lower case** — `'A'` and `'a'` are different characters.
**Building the string with `+=` in a loop** — fine in JavaScript and with a StringBuilder in Java; avoid repeated string concatenation in Java and C# without one.
**Top K Frequent Elements** — the same counts and buckets, stopping after k values (Heap course).
**Sort Array by Increasing Frequency** — ascending counts, ties by value descending: a two-part key.
**Reorganize String** — arrange so no two neighbours are equal, starting from the counts (Heap course).
